lfl-viewlayer-new-6-7-10.background:
The locality belongs to the Øygarden Complex, which is the basement rocks beneath the allochtonous Bergen Arcs. The faults on Toft are Devonian and relate to the termination of the Caledonian orogeny and following basement exhumation of the metamorphic core complex.

On Toft, we find faults with excelent exposure, which gives us valuable insight into the brittle deformation of the crust. On this locality, we will explore fault kinematics, stress regimes and for those interested we will try to evaluate the regional fault network on Toft, to try to better understand the connection between what is seen in seismic and core data and in the outcrops.
lfl-viewlayer-new-6-7-10.practical:
Avoid hammering to preserve the outcrop!

Take the bus to Svelgen Bru. As of 2026, it is one bus change to a corresponding bus at Ågotnes when travelling from Bergen bus station. It is then a short walk along the road from the bus stop to the outcrop. If arriving by car, there is a large parking space below the outcrop.

Bring a hand lens and a notebook. Bring a compass or the clino app to measure the orientation of the fault.

lfl-viewlayer-new-6-8-11.background: The folds are located in the Øygarden Complex, a near autochtonous metamorphic core complex west of the allochtonous Bergen Arcs consisting of basement gneisses. It has a long and complex deformation history, including both Sveconorwegian and Caledonian deformation phases. The complex underwent major plastic deformation during the collision and collapse of the Caledonian orogeny. This event was later overprinted by brittle deformation during North Sea rifting.
lfl-viewlayer-new-6-8-11.practical:
Avoid hammering to preserve the outcrop!

Take the bus to the Vik bus stop. As of 2026 it is easy to get there from Bergen bus station, with aasf one corresponding bus transfer at Ågotnes Terminal. From there it is a very short walk along the pavement north towards the outcrop, which is easily visible along the road. If arriving by car, there is parking just south of the outcrop.

Bring a hand lens, notebook, pencil and a ruler or yard stick. Bring either a compass with a clinometer or the clino app to take structural measurements. The locality is roadside, and cars go by fast, so bring a reflective vest, and to be careful when crossing the road, and when examining the outcrop. If needed, bring the textbook by Haakon Fossen to assist with classifying the folds.

lfl-viewlayer-new-6-9-12.background:
Spildepollen is located on the northern end of Austefjorden, which follows a NS-striking fault. The fault relates to the stretching and thinning of the North Sea crust, which formed many shoreline parallel faults. A series of Late Permian dikes intrudes the area around Spildepollen.

Geologically, this area is part of the Øygarden Complex, which is parautochtonous basement, structurally lower than the allochtonous Bergen Arcs. It is exposed as a metamorphic core complex.
lfl-viewlayer-new-6-9-12.practical:
Avoid hammering to preserve the outcrop!

The locality is on the north end of Austefjorden, at Spildepollen. Take the bus to the Spildepollen bus stop. The locality is very near the bus stop, along the roadcut east of the roundabout. The

lfl-viewlayer-new-6-10-13.background: The locality belongs to the allochtonous Minor Bergen Arc. Tectonostratigraphically it is part of the ophiolitic terrane of the upper allochton in the Norwegian Caledonides. The exposed rocks are upper basement rocks along the basal Caledonian thrust. It is believed that this thrust was reactivated during the Caledonian collapse.
lfl-viewlayer-new-6-10-13.practical:
Avoid hammering to preserve this excellent outcrop!

Verftet is central in Bergen, and easily accessible from Realfagsbygget. Walk towards Nordnes and head down to Georgernes Verft. The outcrop is exposed on the right-hand side before the large apartment complexes, near the seaside. The walk is easy and the outcrop is accessible for all along a paved road.

Bring a hand lens, pencils, a notebook and a compass with a clinometer or the clino app.

lfl-viewlayer-new-6-17-14.background: The conglomerate found at the top of Sandviksfjellet consists of a spectacular strained conglomerate relating to the Caledonian orogeny and collapse. The locality is ideal for understanding strain in the allochtons of the Norwegian Caledonides, strain analysis and to gain insights into the sedimentation in the Iapetus Ocean. Do not hammer on this outcrop to preserve the locality!
lfl-viewlayer-new-6-17-14.practical: The field trip starts at Sandviken Sykehus. Take the bus north from the city centre to Munkebotn. See the “Skyss” app for travel options. Once there, walk past the hospital up Munkebotn. Walk the paved road to the top of the dam, keeping in mind the changing bedrock outcrops along the road, taking note of the lithology. Once you reach the dam, turn left and walk the small bridge that crosses the rived ahead, once again keeping note of the lithology. Keep walking up the trail until you are almost at Sandvikshytten. There you will find a smaller trail heading right. Take this, and the conglomerate will be clearly visible after about 50 metres.

lfl-viewlayer-new-6-12-15.background: Kleppestø sits at the Bergen Detachment shear zone, nestled between the autochtonous Proterozoic basement of the Øygarden Complex and the allochtonous Bergen Arcs. It therefore represents an area of very high localised strain. The Bergen Detachment had a major deformation phase during the Devonian relating to the exhumation of the Øygarden Complex. Kleppestø is therefore a great locality to study the post-collisional evolution of the Caledonian nappes surrounding Bergen.
lfl-viewlayer-new-6-12-15.practical:
Avoid hammering to preserve the outcrop!

Kleppestø might seem far out from Bergen but it is easily accessible by a ferry which is covered by the Skyss ticket. The ferry leaves from Strandkaiterminalen, near Bryggen, and arrives at Kleppestø kai. From there it is a short walk to the outcrop. See “Skyss” for travel times.

The outcrop is roadside and easily accessible. It in a roadcut at a turn, and is bordered by cross-walks on each side.

Kleppestø is therefore a great locality to study the post-collisional evolution of the Caledonian nappes surrounding Bergen.

Kleppestø might seem far out from Bergen but it is easily accessible by a ferry which is covered by the Skyss ticket. The ferry leaves from Strandkaiterminalen, near Bryggen, and arrives at Kleppestø kai. From there it is a short walk to the outcrop. See “Skyss” for travel times.

The outcrop is roadside and easily accessible.

lfl-viewlayer-new-6-18-17.background: Helleneset is located in the Blåmanen Nappe of the Bergen Arcs, in what is known as the Biskopshavn Migmatite Complex of the Ulriken Gneiss Complex. It is essentially a Precambrian migmatite complex that has been sheared during the main phase of continent-continent collision in the Caledonian orogeny, the Scandian event.
lfl-viewlayer-new-6-18-17.practical:
Avoid hammering to preserve the outcrop!

Helleneset is easily accessible from the city centre. It is possible to walk there, but it is perhaps more convinient to take the bus. The closest bus stop is called Hellebakken. Check “Skyss” for information.

The locality is found in a park. Walk down towards the beach, and head left towards the swimming pool. The locality can be defined from between the gazebo and all the way to the ocean past the swimming pool.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-2-3.background: Geohazards are events that can cause damage to people and infrastructure. They are caused by natural processes or conditions. Along Løvstien there have been multiple geohazard events, some of the recorded events were in 2021 and in 2018. Mitigations have been done along the path to minimize the risk of new events.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-2-3.practical: The field trip starts at the Blekenberg bus stop. Take the bus to this stop or take the Bybane to Danmarks plass and walk up to the bus stop. See the “Skyss” app for travel options. Once at the bus stop follow the signs to Løvstien/Løvstakken. When you come to the path follow Løvstien towards south. When you get to the lean-to you can follow the path approximately 100 meters down and look up at the location, but there can be some trees blocking the view. The other option is to follow the green fence that starts before the lean-to, and follow the fence approximately 100 meters til you get to the location. But be careful there are some loose rocks in the area. If you are short on time you dont need to walk the whole Løvstien, there are several paths you can follow down before the end.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-6-7.background: Geohazards are events that can cause damage to infrastructure and people, floods are one type of geohazards. Starefossen is a waterfall located in a neighbourhood over Kalfaret in Bergen, so when the river floods it impacts the people living in the area. During 2018 the river below Starefossen flooded several times, leading to damages on infrastructure in the area. To try to minimize the damages during flooding events some mitigation in the area have been done.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-6-7.practical: The field trip starts at Starefossen bus stop. Take the 11 bus from the city centre. See the “Skyss” app for travel times. Once there, walk down the road past the kindergarten. Once past the kindergarten follow the path up towards the waterfall (Starefossen). When you are at the point where the water stream flows under the path, go off the path up to Starefossen.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-8-8.background: During the glaciations glaciers have eroded and formed the landscape, Hardbakkedalen was formed through these glaciations. Landforms and deposits can tell us about how the glaciers have eroded and formed landscape and how the glaciers have moved. In Hardbakkedalen you can find a glaciated valley and some signs after the glaciation.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-8-8.practical: The field trip starts at Trekantparken. Take the bus to Svartediksveien or Årstadveien, both are by Trekantparken. See the “Skyss” app for travel options. Once there, follow the signs to Tarlebøveien along Svartediksveien. Follow Tarlebøveien along Svartediket. Take the path up towards Hardbakkedalen, when you see the signs to Hardbakkedalen. When the path flattens you will find Location 1, a rounded rock outcrop. To get to location 2 follow the path further to you get to a good viewing point of the valley.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-9-9.background: Landforms and their formation process is important to understand. Since they can tell us a lot about how the climate and deposital environments have been in the past. There we can use modern depositional environments we see today to get an indication on how different deposits were deposited in the past. Here you will see different landforms, some deposits are from the last ice age and some are not related to glaciers. Remember that it is important to separate descriptions and interpretations.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-9-9.practical: The field trip starts at the Herdla sør bus stop. Take the 400 bus from Bergen busstasjon to Ravanger terminal. At Ravanger terminal change to the 414 bus to Herdla and get off at Herdla Museet. See the “Skyss” app for travel times. Once there, walk up the Herdleåsen road. Take the first road to the left and follow that until there is a path on the right side of the road, down to a small beach. Stop 1 is at the rock outcrop at the southern side of the beach. Stop 2 is the rock outcrop sticking up in the middle of the beach. Stop 3 is in the sediment outcrop at the back of the beach. Stop 4 is in the slope behind the beach. To get to stop 5 you need to go back up to the road and follow it further until you come to a beach with a lot of big boulders. It is recommended to bring a trowel, knife or similar tool. to get clean sediment outcrops.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-10-10.background: After the glacial periods the sea level at Herdla has varied. The different beach deposits can be studied at the southwestern side of Herdla. The beach sediments observed at today's beaches can give us insight into how the sea level and deposition environments have varied in the past. Therefore it is important to understand the deposition environments of today to better understand the past depositions.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-10-10.practical: The field trip starts at the Herdla sør bus stop. Take the 400 bus from Bergen busstasjon to Ravanger terminal. At Ravanger terminal change to the 414 bus to Herdla and go off at Herdla sør. See the “Skyss” app for travel times. Once there, walk towards the golf course and walk down the gravel road by the “Herdla Golf” sign. Follow the gravel road until you come to the slope, take the path down to the beach. Stop 1 is at the beach. Stop 2 you can find multiple sediment outcrops in the slope. It is important that you choose an outcrop that has a black layer in it. Stop 3 is a little more towards the south end of the beach, where you will find outcrops with more sand. It is recommended to bring a trowel or knife to get clean outcrops.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-12-11.background: During Younger Dryas the Scandinavian Ice Sheet expanded out to Western Norway. At Ulvensletta you can find landforms from this time. During the advance in Os the glacier came from Northeast and moved Southwest towards Ulven. The glacier advanced changed where the sediments deposited, before the advance the sediments got deposited in Fusafjorden.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-12-11.practical: The field trip starts at the Grindevoll snuplass. Take the bus to Grindevoll snuplass or Grindevoll and walk up to the Grindevoll snuplass. See the “Skyss” app for travel options. Once there take follow the tractor road approximately 150 meters till stop 1, here you must find a good sediment outcrop on the right side of the road. To get to stop 2 you can either walk approximaly 40 minutes to Os Aero Klubb or take the buss to Ulvensletta and have a short walk to Os Aero Klubb. Once there follow the small gravel road northeast. Stop 2 is the whole flat area. Stop 3 is the pile on the left side of the road, right after the road barrier.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-13-12.background: Krohnegården is a recreation area in Bergen, but if you investigate the landforms you will see that there are some glacial landforms in the area. These landforms tell us that this area has been glaciated, and they can tell us something about the glaciation in the area. By using LiDAR and field observations it is possible to identify glacial landforms.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-13-12.practical: The field trip starts at the Skytebanen bus stop. You can take the bus to this bus stop or take the bus to Løvstakkskiftet and walk to the skytebanen bus stop. See the “Skyss” app for travel options. Follow the gravel road up until a steep part approximately 150 meters, here stop 1 is located. Look for some sediment outcrops. To get to stop 2, follow the gravel road back and follow the road south, here you will find the area on the right side of the road. Stop 3 is in the same area as stop 2, but there is a path towards north that takes you back towards Løvstakkskiftet. Look for big boulders along the path.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-14-13.background: During the glaciations glaciers have eroded and formed landscapes, Jordal is a valley formed through these glaciations. Landforms and deposits can tell us about how the glaciers have eroded and formed landscape, they can also give insights off how the glaciers have moved.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-14-13.practical: The field trip starts at the bus stop Jordal snuplass. Take the bus to Jordal snuplass. See the “Skyss” app for travel options. Once there, follow the road over the small bridge and take the first road to the right. Follow the road until a small tractor road, follow this road to the gate and take the path on the other side. Stop 1 is on the left side of the path, after the gate. Where there are some sediment outcrops. To get to stop 2 follow the path, the stop is at Stallane where you get a nice view of Jordal. Follow the gravel road from Stallane until you get to Vinddalsveien, and follow the road to the right. Stop 3 is in the valley where you get a good view of it. Stop 4 is located in the area where you entered Vinddalsveien. There will be some hiking on this field trip so bring good shoes.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-15-14.background: During the glaciations glaciers have eroded and formed landscapes. On Blåmanen there are signs after the glaciations. These signs after the glaciers can give information about the movement of the glacier and when they disappeared.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-15-14.practical: The field trip starts at Fløyen, you can either walk up from the city centre or take the tram up. Follow the gravel road with signs towards Rundemanen. When you get to Store Tindevatnet you turn off Rundemansveien and take a smaller gravel road towards Blåmanen. Follow this road until it splits into two paths, take the path to the right. Stop 1 is located by the first small lake. The first outcrop is located on the right side of the elevation in the terrain. For task 6 see the marked area in the map for the area you should look in. To get to stop 2 follow the path further, the stop is at the big boulder on the first hilltop. There will be some hiking on this field trip so bring good shoes and clothing for the weather.

lfl-viewlayer-new-7-16-15.background: In 2018 the dam at munkebotsvatnet were being built, during the construction of the dam a temporary dam was built. During the construction of the new dam a period with high precipitation led to that the temporary dam overflowed and it was breached. This led to a large release of water, and a flooding downstream. The flood led to evacuation of Eidsvåg and closing of roads downstream. The flooding lead to damages in infrastructure but luckily no persons were harmed in the flood. This flood is an example of a geohazard that led to damage on infrastructure, and give a insight on how floods can cause damage.
lfl-viewlayer-new-7-16-15.practical: The field trip starts at Gamle Bergen bus stop. See the “Skyss” app for travel times. Once there, follow Sandviksleitet alongside Sandviken hospital. At the end of the road there is a path on the right side of the road, that leads to road that leads to Munkebotsvatnet. When you get to the lake, follow it to the northern side where the dam is. This is the start of the field trip, then follow the river down.
